neighbours.label: the period of the title 'Mrs.' before a name, as against the periods of 'Mr.', 'Ms.', 'Dr.', 'St.' and sentence-final periods
fire: At the bakery on Elm Street, Mrs. Romero sells the best bread in town.
Our first piano teacher was Mrs. Kowalski, who lived above the shop.
The play opens with Mrs. Higgins reading a letter in her garden.
Every winter the church choir is led by Mrs. Oduya.
I still remember how Mrs. Chen explained fractions with apples.
In the novel, Mrs. Bennet worries about her daughters' marriages.
The award was presented by Mrs. Lindqvist, the school principal.
Next door lived Mrs. Abernathy and her three noisy dogs.
quiet: At the bakery on Elm Street, Mr. Romero sells the best bread in town.
Our first piano teacher was Ms. Kowalski, who lived above the shop.
The play opens with Dr. Higgins reading a letter in his garden.
Every winter the church choir is led by our vicar. She sings well.
I still remember how Prof. Chen explained fractions with apples.
In the novel, Mr. Bennet laughs at his daughters' worries.
The award was presented by Gen. Lindqvist, the base commander.
Next door lived St. John and his three noisy dogs, or so we joked.
